---
title: "Error budgets under estimated pairwise probabilities"
subtitle: "4.14 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 15"
description: "How a bound on Monte Carlo error changes which reports can satisfy an error budget."
---

An error budget caps the expected share of wrong stated directions. A report may pass that budget when we use
estimated probabilities and fail it under the exact probabilities. A uniform error bound lets us use a tighter
estimated budget to find reports that definitely pass, and a looser one to retain every report that passes.
We check the bound and both claims about the report sets separately. A separate fixed-size simulation shows
how often a bound of this kind can hold over repeated draws from the same law.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Estimated pass.** For A above B, the estimated wrong share is .200 and the exact supplied-law share is .300.
  The budget is .25. The estimate passes and the exact probability fails. The number line shows the tighter threshold .15 and
  looser threshold .35.
- **Negative inner.** The signed inner threshold is −.05, even though the estimated wrong share is 0. Replacing
  this threshold with zero would wrongly admit A above B. The all-withheld report still passes the count-form
  tests, with no defined wrong share.
- **Exactly two.** Requiring two grades removes all-withheld. The inner family has 0 reports; the exact family
  also happens to be empty here. Their separate counters matter: an empty inner family alone would not establish
  exact infeasibility.
- **Radius too small.** The proposed radius is reduced to .05 with the exact law unchanged.
  The coefficient checks read “no,” and an inner member fails the exact budget. The report that passes the tighter estimate but fails the exact budget is shown in the table.
- **Raw comparisons.** With advisory tolerance removed, its coefficient check reads “no.” At the default radius,
  the tiny raw excess explains why the strict check fails while the tolerant comparison passes. The actual
  inclusions are separate tests, not consequences of accepting a soft tolerance.
- **Fixed-S IID.** The simulation uses 1,000 complete states drawn from the independent normal posteriors for six sites. Score B has error weight 0 but remains protected by its .03
  budget. Requiring exactly two grades gives an empty inner family while the exact family remains nonempty.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The two-unit example specifies the exact and estimated probabilities directly. In the simulation, the chance
that all estimated coefficients fall within the bound is at least one minus α across repeated samples of the
same size from the same law. This probability describes the numerical estimates under that law. Compliance
under the model is still determined by the exact expected wrong share. The thresholds can be negative.
:::
